title.narrative: Lifesaving assistance to displaced populations in the Far-North, Northwest and Southwest Regions of Cameroon through emergency shelters and NFIs

description.narrative: The overall objective of this project is to contribute to improve displaced populations’ living conditions, dignity and save lives through the distribution of emergency shelter and non-food items (NFI) in the Far North (FN), Northwest (NW) and Southwest (SW) regions of Cameroon. In the FN region, ongoing socio-political crisis have heavily impacted local populations, where displacements are still triggered due to small scale sporadic attacks by non-state armed groups as well as seasonal floods. According to the OCHA flood information note of 19 September 2024, at least 365,060 people have been affected by flooding in 5 Far North departments: Logone and Chari, Mayo-Danay, Diamaré, Mayo-Tsanaga and Mayo-Kani. Mayo Danay and Logone and Chari are the most affected departments, with 193,892 and 146,224 people affected respectively. At least 30 people died, more than 56,084 houses were partially or totally destroyed, 82,509 hectares of arable land were flooded (54,094 in Mayo-Danay and 27,653 in Logone and Chari), 5,278 head of livestock were lost and around 262 educational structures were affected by the floods. The affected communities have major needs in various sectors ranked by priority as follows: nutrition, shelter and NFIs, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), health, education, and protection. There is also a critical need to reinforce the capacities of implementing partners to provide rapid humanitarian assistance in FN and NW, SW.The ongoing socio-political crisis in the NW and SW regions continues to trigger massive internal displacement, with 14,812 households (6,524 internally displaced households, 6,602 returnees households and 1,686 host community households),e in search of security and shelter in the bushes or surrounding communities from multisectoral needs assessment (MSNA), (IOM, September 2024). The violence also puts further pressure on communities in vulnerable situations, including those in hard-to-reach locations. IOM plans to respond to the most urgent and essential needs in shelter and NFIs of displaced and vulnerable populations in these areas, while mitigating the pressure on host communities. In this project, using the household average of 5.5 obtained from the latest multisectoral needs assessment (IOM, August 2024) to all 1,665 displaced households, IOM will provide emergency shelters and conditional cash assistance for NFIs both in FN (1265 HH) and NWSW (400 HH) for a total of 9,150 persons (1665 households) Emergency shelters are designed to build a self-standing shelter in accordance with the Shelter Cluster. The shelters are intended to be light and mobile for high humanitarian access and quick installation. Shelters are provided to the most vulnerable individuals who have been recently displaced and lack adequate housing, whether they have no shelter at all or are living in substandard conditions. This support is complemented by technical assistance to beneficiaries, focusing on construction techniques and maintenance methods to enable them to maintain their shelters effectively and efficiently. Therefore, the selection of the vulnerable households is protection centered and will apply a gender sensitive lens and ensure disability inclusion to guarantee the most vulnerable individuals who face higher protection risk benefit from assistance.
